words.dev.built.body: Personal chats and private groups are end-to-end encrypted, while communities, open rooms and status are not, and each one tells you which it is before you post. AChat runs on the web and Android from one codebase.
words.dev.contact.body: Questions about AChat go through the contact page.
words.dev.for.body: Ahsan reads AChat as three products under one name. Anonymous rooms came first: open a room by a simple link, with or without a temporary password, share text or a file, then delete the room or keep it. Then everyday messaging with friends and family, where changing phones must never cost you your chats. Then chat you can embed in your own website. The aim is simple. Everything to do with talking by chat.
words.dev.gaps.body: Anonymous rooms are here, and personal chats are end-to-end encrypted. Embedding covers rooms and open channels, not a support inbox yet. If you lose every device and your recovery key, your encrypted history is gone today; a way to get it back after signing in is being built. There are no calls yet.
words.dev.j1: Work on AChat begins, with anonymous rooms.
words.dev.j2: The rebuild starts, from an approved prototype of every screen.
words.dev.j3: The rebuilt AChat goes live on the web, with earlier rooms carried across.
words.dev.j5: Speak, Draft help and Catch me up arrive.
words.dev.j6: Two-step sign-in, recovery codes, and an API and MCP server for other apps.
words.dev.lead: Ahsan Mahmood (aoneahsan) started AChat to move a password or a file between his own computers without signing in to anything on the one that needed it. It grew from there.
